name: relion.reconstructparticletomo
label: Relion Tomo Reconstruct Particles
help: RELION subtomogram particle reconstruction (Reconstruct): relion_tomo_reconstruct_particle builds high-resolution 3D maps directly from tilt series using an optimisation set or direct tomography inputs. Matches RelionJob::initialiseTomoReconPartJob.

params.name: in_optimisation
params.label: Input optimisation set:
params.help: Input optimisation set. This will be passed with a --i argument to relion_tomo_reconstruct_particle. If any individual components of the optimisation set are specified below, then they will override the components in this optimisation set.

params.name: use_direct_entries
params.label: OR: use direct entries?
params.help: If set to Yes, the optimisation set will be ignored and the direct entries below will be used instead.

params.name: in_tomograms
params.label: Input tomogram set:
params.help: Input tomogram set STAR file. This file gets generated during Tomogram Reconstruction, and updated during Tomogram Frame Alignment or Tomogram CTF Refinement.

params.name: in_trajectories
params.label: Input trajectory set:
params.help: Input trajectory set. Leave empty if no particle motion tracks have been estimated during tomogram frame alignment.

params.name: binning
params.label: Binning factor:
params.help: The tilt series images will be binned by this (real-valued) factor and then reconstructed in the specified box size above. Note that thereby the reconstructed region becomes larger when specifying binning factors larger than one.

params.name: box_size
params.label: Box size (binned pix):
params.help: Box size of the reconstruction. Note that this is independent of the box size that has been used to refine the particle. This allows the user to construct a 3D map of arbitrary size to gain an overview of the structure surrounding the particle. A sufficiently large box size also allows more of the high-frequency signal to be captured that has been delocalised by the CTF.

params.name: crop_size
params.label: Cropped box size (binned pix):
params.help: If set to a positive value, the program will output an additional set of maps that have been cropped to this size. This is useful if a map is desired that is smaller than the box size required to retrieve the CTF-delocalised signal.

params.name: snr
params.label: Wiener SNR constant:
params.help: If set to a positive value, apply a Wiener filter with this signal-to-noise ratio. If omitted, the reconstruction will use a heuristic to prevent divisions by excessively small numbers. Please note that using a low (even though realistic) SNR might wash out the higher frequencies, which could make the map unsuitable to be used for further refinement.

params.name: sym_name
params.label: Symmetry:
params.help:
If the molecule is asymmetric, set Symmetry group to C1. Note their are multiple possibilities for icosahedral symmetry: 
 * I1: No-Crowther 222 (standard in Heymann, Chagoyen & Belnap, JSB, 151 (2005) 196–207) 
 * I2: Crowther 222 
 * I3: 52-setting (as used in SPIDER?)
 * I4: A different 52 setting 
 The command 'relion_refine --sym D2 --print_symmetry_ops' prints a list of all symmetry operators for symmetry group D2. RELION uses XMIPP's libraries for symmetry operations. Therefore, look at the XMIPP Wiki for more details:  http://xmipp.cnb.csic.es/twiki/bin/view/Xmipp/WebHome?topic=Symmetry

params.name: nr_mpi
params.label: Number of MPI procs:
params.help: Number of MPI nodes to use in parallel. When set to 1, MPI will not be used. The maximum can be set through the environment variable RELION_MPI_MAX.

params.name: nr_threads
params.label: Number of threads:
params.help: Number of shared-memory (POSIX) threads to use in parallel. When set to 1, no multi-threading will be used. The maximum can be set through the environment variable RELION_THREAD_MAX.

params.name: other_args
params.label: Additional arguments:
params.help: In this box command-line arguments may be provided that are not generated by the GUI. This may be useful for testing developmental options and/or expert use of the program. To print a list of possible options, run the corresponding program from the command line without any arguments.
